reviews.review: Just not a good game, spend your money elsewhere
Pretty much Left for dead 3. Fun game

Contrary to what most people think, Back 4 Blood is a really engaging zombie shooter game, part of the same family as the Left 4 Dead games, but totally a different game and definitely not Left 4 Dead 3. I don't get the hatred the game gets since nothing is wrong with it from my point of view, and there are numerous aspects to appreciate, such as: a variety of maps, diverse enemies that come in multiple variations, an extensive arsenal of weapons that can be upgraded and personalized, and every single game is different thanks to the card system that introduces significant variety and randomness, ensuring each game feels unique. Playing with friends is a great way to explore the game's offerings and can help the player learn the game's core mechanics quickly.

The card system might seem complex to newbie players, as do most mechanics in the game, but once you understand how it works, you quickly realize how much variety these cards can offer to the game, and you are free to personalize your game experience and get some unique perks during the game depending on your play style. If you are not satisfied with your cards, you can create a new deck anytime to experience different scenarios and enhance the game's variety. As a veteran of the Left 4 Dead series with 4000 hours played in both games, I can attest that Back 4 Blood offers more variety in this aspect. However, what this game is missing, unlike Left 4 Dead games, are the characters' personalities, the immersive small details, the dark vibe of the maps, and personally, the fact that you're not affected by common infected attacks such as camera shaking, and you may realize too late that you are being attacked by an entire horde behind your back.

The campaigns in Back 4 Blood are distinct, each coming with unique objectives and different enemies. There are scripted events you are aware of and sometimes you face unexpected challenges introduced by the random corrupt cards that might occur during your game. The DLCs are worth playing, especially the Ridden Hives, but they are overpriced in my opinion, and they could be easily introduced to the game as an update instead of a pack of DLCs. I think that this game feels bad to newbie players coming from Left 4 Dead games at the beginning, but it gets better the more you play it, discover its beauty, and once you realize that this is not a Left 4 Dead game, but a spiritual successor in some way. I'd like to conclude this review with my favorite quote from my friend suniki's review for Back 4 Blood: "I believe we should judge things for what they are and not what they aren't. By doing so, the argument that it isn't Left 4 Dead 3 partially falls apart."

The gameplay sucks. Its literally just cosmetics and bland hack n slash. No dismemberment, no cool effects, just a body limply falling over after dying. I have no idea whats going on in "campaign" there is no story to follow. Then i found out after buying the game that it wasnt even made by valve. RIP. Ill just go play LFD2 again.
